content.comment_body: Hello [user_name], I encountered a similar issue when a client had trouble using the cursor keys with the system we used before the [product_name] Operator Device was available. Our original setup was designed for [article_no]. Since switching to the [product_name] Operator Device, which benefits from convenient 'one touch' function keys, I'm now interested in disabling the cursor, esc, and ok keys to prevent client access to program controls such as start/stop. Does anyone know if this can be achieved? Thank you
Hello [user_name], Unfortunately, this is not possible! Best regards [user_name]
Have you considered the [product_name] Pure version? It doesn't include any cursor keys.

analysis.insight_summary: Users are seeking ways to restrict access to specific hardware buttons (cursor, esc, ok) on the [product_name] Operator Device to prevent clients from accessing key program functions. Current product features do not allow for disabling these buttons. The community mentions alternative hardware variants without certain keys, but these may not entirely meet user requirements. Positive feedback is noted regarding the 'one touch' function key design for improved usability.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect to be able to deactivate hardware buttons (cursor, esc, ok) on the [product_name] Operator Device, aiming to improve security and limit unwanted client access to essential controls.
